question: Why is training local mothers as peer educators so effective in stopping harmful food taboos?

options.A: Mothers are legally required by the state to teach nutrition classes
options.B: Peer educators have advanced university degrees in clinical medicine
options.C: Mothers listen to fellow community peers who share similar daily life experiences
options.D: Peer educators receive a high monthly salary from international donors

explanation: People are much more likely to adopt new health habits when taught by trusted neighbors from their own background rather than outsiders.

question: Which popular fruit juice is well known for interfering with gut enzymes and dangerously raising blood levels of certain drugs?

options.A: Grapefruit juice
options.B: Filtered tap water
options.C: Fresh cow milk
options.D: Green tea infusion

explanation: Grapefruit juice is a classic pharmacological troublemaker! It blocks specific enzymes in your gut, letting way too much of a drug slip into your bloodstream. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is a major challenge when doing sterile procedures in a patient's home?

options.A: Finding a completely clean surface to set up sterile equipment
options.B: Needing a specialized hospital operating table for every task
options.C: Preventing family members from assisting with the procedure
options.D: Having too many doctors present during the dressing change

explanation: Spot on! Houses don't come pre-sterilized like hospital rooms. As a nurse, you have to create your own clean barrier to keep your sterile supplies safe from everyday household surfaces.

question: How can community leaders help improve low immunization uptake in rural areas?

options.A: By importing vaccines directly from international manufacturers
options.B: By taking over clinical duties and injecting vaccines themselves
options.C: By replacing the cold chain refrigerators with local coolers
options.D: By building trust and addressing local rumors or hesitancy

explanation: Local chiefs and religious leaders have powerful voices. When they support immunization, community members feel much more confident bringing their babies in.

question: What is the most common early sign of endometrial cancer?

options.A: Postmenopausal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Swelling in both lower legs
options.C: Severe lower back pain
options.D: Rapid unintended weight loss

explanation: You nailed it! Any bleeding or spotting after menopause is a red flag that always needs a doctor's attention.

question: Why is the pelvic floor shaped like a hammock?

options.A: To store excess fat reserves in the lower pelvis
options.B: To completely block all pelvic openings at rest
options.C: To anchor the major bones of the lower limbs
options.D: To support abdominal organs against downward pressure

explanation: Spot on! Just like a hammock catches you when you sit, your pelvic floor muscles hold up organs like the bladder and uterus against gravity.

question: Why is it best to count a patient's breathing rate discreetly without telling them right away?

options.A: It saves time during a busy hospital shift to count during pulse checks
options.B: Patients will feel anxious if they know their lungs are being watched
options.C: Unconscious patients are the only ones who have true resting rates
options.D: Conscious awareness can alter the patient's normal breathing rate and depth

explanation: When people know you are watching them breathe, they naturally start controlling it. Counting while pretending to check the pulse is a smart clinical trick! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which outside group is most important for a school to partner with when planning student immunizations?

options.A: International tourism boards
options.B: Local primary healthcare centres
options.C: Private transport unions
options.D: Commercial real estate developers

explanation: You got it! Local health clinics are our go-to partners because they provide the trained staff and vaccines for school immunization drives.

question: What is a very common, mild side effect of most oral deworming drugs?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Transient abdominal discomfort and nausea
options.C: Sudden severe bone fractures
options.D: Permanent loss of hearing acuity

explanation: Totally normal! A little tummy upset or mild nausea can happen as the medication goes to work in the digestive tract.

question: Which developmental process is disrupted in a patient with achondroplasia (a common type of dwarfism)?

options.A: Appositional growth along the periosteum
options.B: Intramembranous ossification of the clavicles
options.C: Endochondral ossification at the epiphyseal plates
options.D: Synovial joint cavity formation in the limbs

explanation: In achondroplasia, the cartilage at the growth plates has trouble converting into bone, which specifically slows down the lengthening of the arms and legs.

question: What is the main goal of teamwork between government health structures and NGOs?

options.A: To eliminate the need for community health nurses in rural clinics
options.B: To ensure NGOs take over full ownership of the Ministry of Health
options.C: To increase taxes collected from vulnerable patients
options.D: To combine resources and prevent duplication of health services

explanation: Working together stops everyone from doing the same job twice! It pools resources so health care reaches more people smoothly.

question: A nurse suspects a patient's injuries are from domestic abuse, but the patient is too scared to talk. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Provide a safe, private environment and gently encourage the patient to talk
options.B: Ignore the suspicion because the patient did not report it directly
options.C: Discharge the patient quickly to avoid getting involved in legal matters
options.D: Call the police immediately and force the patient to make a public statement

explanation: Wonderful! Building trust in a warm, confidential space gives frightened patients the courage to open up at their own pace.

question: Which major organ system is most immediately threatened by severe hyperkalemia (high blood potassium)?

options.A: Skeletal muscle system
options.B: Gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Cardiovascular system
options.D: Integumentary system

explanation: High potassium levels dangerously alter the electrical conduction of the heart, leading to fatal arrhythmias. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why do health workers draw an epidemic curve on a graph during an outbreak?

options.A: To show the timeline of when cases occurred and track the outbreak's progress
options.B: To prove to international donors that funding was spent wisely
options.C: To measure the physical distance between houses in the village
options.D: To predict exactly what the weather will be like next week

explanation: Brilliant! An epidemic curve turns dates into a picture, helping investigators see when infections started and whether the outbreak is slowing down or growing.

question: When would you choose dry heat sterilization instead of an autoclave?

options.A: When processing large batches of surgical metal instruments quickly
options.B: When performing rapid bedside sterilization of open wounds
options.C: When dealing with heat-sensitive plastics and rubber tubing
options.D: When sterilizing powders, oils, or glassware that moisture could ruin

explanation: Dry heat is perfect for things like powders and oils where the wet steam of an autoclave would totally ruin them.

question: What is the single most important and effective step when trying to resuscitate a newborn?

options.A: Giving emergency IV drugs
options.B: Ventilating the newborn's lungs with air or oxygen
options.C: Giving a quick fluid drip
options.D: Doing chest compressions

explanation: Most newborn emergencies happen because they aren't breathing. Getting oxygen into their lungs is always our top rescue step!

question: Why is secondary adrenal insufficiency caused by pituitary problems so dangerous for a patient?

options.A: Blood sugar shoots up dangerously high because of a lack of balance.
options.B: The kidneys suddenly stop filtering waste products out of the blood.
options.C: Lacking ACTH makes the adrenal glands stop producing vital cortisol.
options.D: The heart rate goes completely out of control without nerve signals.

explanation: Without ACTH telling them what to do, the adrenal glands shrink and stop making cortisol. That leaves the body completely unable to handle stress, which can quickly lead to shock.

question: Why are peer educators so helpful in community health outreach?

options.A: They share similar backgrounds and age groups with the target audience, reducing stigma
options.B: They possess advanced medical degrees in obstetrics and gynecology
options.C: They operate exclusively inside high-security government hospitals
options.D: They have legal authority to prescribe restricted pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Well reasoned! Peer educators talk without judgment, making it way easier for young people to open up and connect.

question: Which level of measurement has a true zero point that means none of the item is present?

options.A: Ordinal
options.B: Nominal
options.C: Interval
options.D: Ratio

explanation: Great thinking! Ratio data has an absolute zero—meaning zero actually means none, like a pulse rate of zero. If it's zero, it's completely gone!

question: Why does severe dehydration eventually cause organs to stop working in a child?

options.A: Electrolyte imbalances cause immediate paralysis of the heart
options.B: The kidneys stop working because they are overworked by toxins
options.C: Reduced blood volume leads to poor oxygen delivery to tissues
options.D: The digestive tract bursts from lack of internal pressure

explanation: Think of blood like a delivery truck carrying oxygen. When water is lost, total blood volume drops, meaning vital organs don't get the oxygen they need to keep running smoothly.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four key elements needed to prove malpractice?

options.A: Guilt
options.B: Damages
options.C: Duty
options.D: Breach

explanation: To prove malpractice, you need duty, breach, causation, and damages. 'Guilt' belongs in criminal law, not civil malpractice cases.

question: Why is it important to ask a patient about their current medications during a neuro history?

options.A: Medications completely cure all neurological disorders
options.B: Many drugs can alter mental status or cause tremors
options.C: Pharmaceutical records replace physical examinations
options.D: Drugs are the only cause of sudden vision loss

explanation: Certain drugs and everyday meds can make a patient feel confused or cause shaky hands, which can easily look like a brain problem if you don't check their drug history.

question: What is the primary purpose of giving intravenous fluids in Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: To raise blood pressure to normal levels
options.B: To shrink the size of the primary tumor
options.C: To flush out uric acid and protect the kidneys
options.D: To replace lost red blood cells

explanation: Aggressive hydration forces urine production, helping the kidneys wash away dangerous breakdown products like uric acid and potassium. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which essential vitamin is manufactured by the friendly bacteria living in our large intestine?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Vitamin K
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Vitamin D

explanation: That's correct! Our gut microbes are great roommates—they help us out by making vitamin K, which is vital for normal blood clotting.

question: What is the primary purpose of a needle holder during wound closure?

options.A: To clamp bleeding blood vessels in the subcutaneous fat
options.B: To pull back skin edges for a better view of the muscle
options.C: To cut excess suture thread after the knot is tied
options.D: To firmly grip the needle and drive it through tissue safely

explanation: Needle holders provide a strong, stable grip so the surgeon can guide the needle through tough layers without slipping. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h7)

question: What defines a mass casualty incident (MCI)?

options.A: An emergency that only happens inside a surgical theatre
options.B: A routine medical ward shift with high patient turnover
options.C: Any situation where a single patient arrives in an ambulance
options.D: Patient numbers and injuries overwhelm available local resources

explanation: An MCI happens when the scale of the emergency outstrips the normal staff, space, and supplies of the hospital or clinic. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h6)

question: What happens in the body when there aren't enough antioxidant micronutrients to protect the cells?

options.A: Enhanced cell membrane stability
options.B: Immediate hormone hypersecretion
options.C: Rapid muscle fiber regeneration
options.D: Oxidative stress and cell damage

explanation: Well done! Without antioxidants to keep harmful free radicals in check, those unstable molecules cause tissue wear-and-tear and lead to long-term health issues.

question: Which animal is the very first home (intermediate host) for the Paragonimus parasite?

options.A: Domestic pig
options.B: Aquatic bird
options.C: Freshwater crab
options.D: Freshwater snail

explanation: Great job! The parasite's early larvae need to enter a freshwater snail first to grow and develop through their early stages.

question: What is the correct order of the three stages in Hans Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome?

options.A: Alarm, exhaustion, resistance
options.B: Alarm, resistance, exhaustion
options.C: Exhaustion, resistance, alarm
options.D: Resistance, alarm, exhaustion

explanation: Think of it as a journey: your body first sounds the alarm when stressed, tries to fight back during resistance, and finally gets worn out in exhaustion if the stress doesn't stop. You've got this!

question: Why are patients who vomit heavily for a long time at high risk for metabolic alkalosis?

options.A: They eat too many alkaline foods while recovering
options.B: Their lungs trap extra carbon dioxide to fix the fluid loss
options.C: Their kidneys completely stop making urine
options.D: They lose large amounts of stomach acid

explanation: Vomiting throws out hydrochloric acid from your stomach, leaving your body with extra base, which pushes your blood pH up into alkalosis.

question: When a patient is newly connected to a ventilator, what is the most common starting PEEP (Positive End-Expiratory Pressure) setting used to keep small air sacs open?

options.A: 20 cmH2O
options.B: 5 cmH2O
options.C: 0 cmH2O
options.D: 50 cmH2O

explanation: A baseline PEEP of 5 cmH2O acts like a gentle cushion at the end of each breath, stopping tiny air sacs (alveoli) from collapsing so breathing stays easier.

question: A patient experiences a sudden seizure that immediately affects both sides of the brain with a total loss of consciousness. How is this classified?

options.A: Peripheral nerve spasm
options.B: Generalized onset seizure
options.C: Localized partial seizure
options.D: Focal aware seizure

explanation: When both brain hemispheres are engaged from the very beginning, the event is classified as a generalized onset seizure. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h3)

question: Why is electrical muscle stimulation sometimes used during physical rehabilitation?

options.A: To permanently replace voluntary muscle contraction
options.B: To help re-educate and stimulate muscles that have lost nerve signaling
options.C: To provide general systemic pain relief like a warm bath
options.D: To rapidly increase red blood cell production

explanation: Spot on! Gentle electrical pulses can help wake up and contract muscles that aren't receiving normal signals from the brain yet.

question: A quiet elderly patient takes a normal sedative before a procedure and suddenly starts shouting. What is your best conclusion?

options.A: The medication dosage was clearly too low to be effective
options.B: The patient has developed an anaphylactic immune reaction
options.C: The patient is experiencing a rare idiosyncratic drug response
options.D: The patient is suffering from acute bacterial meningitis

explanation: Getting wild instead of sleepy from a sedative points right to a paradoxical idiosyncratic reaction. Spot on!

question: When should a nurse refer a patient for genetic counseling regarding cancer?

options.A: The patient has a strong family history suggesting an inherited gene mutation.
options.B: The patient needs immediate chemotherapy for an active lung tumor.
options.C: The patient wants to quit smoking and needs nicotine replacement therapy.
options.D: The patient requires physical therapy to recover from radiation fatigue.

explanation: If a family history points to inherited genes, genetic counseling helps patients understand their risks and plan ahead.

question: At what exact moment during patient care should you sort and throw away your waste?

options.A: At the end of the nursing shift
options.B: When the cleaning crew arrives
options.C: Inside the main hospital furnace room
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Always sort waste right where you use it! Doing it immediately stops accidental mixing and keeps everyone safe from needle pricks later.

question: What is considered the strongest legal defense tool for a nurse facing a malpractice lawsuit?

options.A: Personal memory of busy ward shifts
options.B: Accurate, contemporaneous, and detailed patient records
options.C: Verbal testimony given years after the incident
options.D: Apologizing to the patient's family immediately

explanation: As the saying goes in nursing: if it wasn't charted, it wasn't done! Clear, timely notes are your best protection in court.

question: Where are most private hospitals and well-equipped health facilities concentrated in Nigeria?

options.A: Isolated coastal fishing ports
options.B: Nomadic desert settlements
options.C: Urban centers and major cities
options.D: Remote rural farming villages

explanation: Private investors tend to set up where business is booming, meaning big cities get better equipped facilities than rural areas.

question: Why does a person with iron deficiency anemia look so pale?

options.A: Lack of iron thickens the outer layer of the skin
options.B: Poor circulation causes blood to pool exclusively in deep organs
options.C: Reduced hemoglobin levels decrease the red color of the blood and skin
options.D: The liver stops producing melanin pigments in the skin

explanation: Correct! Hemoglobin is what gives blood its bright red color. When iron is low, hemoglobin drops, and the skin loses that healthy pinkish glow. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the main difference between cancer staging and cancer grading?

options.A: Staging measures how far the cancer has spread, while grading describes how abnormal the cells look
options.B: Staging evaluates treatment side effects, while grading measures tumor size only
options.C: Staging determines the patient's age of onset, while grading determines their genetic risk
options.D: Staging is done exclusively with blood tests, while grading requires a patient interview

explanation: Well done! Think of staging as 'where has it traveled?' and grading as 'how wild and aggressive do the cells look under a microscope?'

question: What is the main difference between an 'adolescent' and 'adolescence'?

options.A: One is the person, and the other is the transitional process
options.B: One applies only to males, and the other only to females
options.C: They are completely identical terms used interchangeably
options.D: One refers to physical growth, and the other to mental illness

explanation: Think of it this way: the adolescent is the human being, and adolescence is the exciting stage of life they are walking through!

question: What three main fields are combined in nursing informatics?

options.A: Public health, sociology, and computer engineering
options.B: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Hospital administration, finance, and nursing
options.D: Biology, chemistry, and clinical pharmacology

explanation: Nursing informatics relies on blending nursing knowledge with computer and information systems to handle clinical data. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a baseline psychiatric assessment for a patient with a degenerative illness?

options.A: To diagnose the exact genetic mutation causing the disease
options.B: To establish a baseline for the patient's mood and cognitive status
options.C: To replace the need for a physical neurological examination
options.D: To test the patient's physical strength and balance

explanation: Taking a baseline measurement lets us see where the patient stands today, so we can track any mental or emotional changes later on.

question: What is a major benefit of using video conferencing for patient follow-up care?

options.A: It bridges geographical gaps for patients in remote areas
options.B: It completely replaces the need for any in-person hospital visits
options.C: It removes all requirements for patient data privacy protection
options.D: It allows nurses to physically change dressings from miles away

explanation: Video tools allow nurses to assess and support patients who live far away without requiring them to travel to the facility. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why does the PMTCT strategy include primary prevention of HIV in women as its first prong?

options.A: Antiretroviral drugs are too expensive to give to pregnant women.
options.B: Men do not play any role in the transmission of the virus.
options.C: Uninfected women of childbearing age cannot transmit a virus they do not have.
options.D: Primary prevention replaces the need for infant diagnostic testing.

explanation: Stopping women from contracting HIV in the first place eliminates the possibility of vertical transmission entirely. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h3)

question: What key lifestyle advice should nurses give to help prevent osteoporosis in postmenopausal women?

options.A: Avoiding exposure to natural sunlight entirely
options.B: Following a strictly low-protein liquid diet
options.C: Restricting all forms of physical activity
options.D: Engaging in regular weight-bearing exercises

explanation: Activities like walking, jogging, or dancing put gentle pressure on bones, signaling them to stay strong and dense!

question: Why do circulating hormones only affect certain specific tissues rather than every cell in the body?

options.A: Only target cells possess the specific receptors for that hormone
options.B: Blood flow is completely blocked from non-target organs
options.C: Hormones are instantly destroyed if they touch wrong cells
options.D: Non-target cells actively repel circulating chemical messengers

explanation: A hormone travels everywhere via the blood, but only cells with matching receptors can receive the message and respond. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h1)

question: How does the parasympathetic system help control your urinary bladder?

options.A: It tightens all sphincters so you never pee
options.B: It relaxes the bladder wall to hold more urine
options.C: It contracts the bladder wall to help you pass urine
options.D: It has no role in urinary control

explanation: Parasympathetic stimulation tells the bladder wall (detrusor muscle) to squeeze and the internal sphincter to relax so urine can flow out. Excellent nursing knowledge!

question: Why do nurses do a 'risk assessment' when they first visit a pregnant woman at home?

options.A: To decide which hospital the baby will attend school
options.B: To find out the exact sex of the unborn baby
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of delivery
options.D: To determine how often the pregnant woman needs monitoring

explanation: Sorting mums by risk helps you know who needs more frequent visits and closer attention. Makes total sense, right?

question: What is the simple difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is used only for animals, while quarantine is used exclusively for human beings.
options.B: Isolation requires medication, while quarantine involves only dietary changes.
options.C: Isolation is voluntary, while quarantine is always legally enforced by police.
options.D: Isolation separates sick people with a disease, while quarantine separates people exposed to a disease who might become sick.

explanation: Remember: Isolation is for those who are *already sick*, while quarantine is for those who were *exposed* and are waiting to see if they'll fall ill.

question: A patient is scheduled for an abdominal CT with IV contrast. What is the very first thing a nurse should check?

options.A: Administer a full dose of oral laxatives to clear the bowel
options.B: Assess the patient for a history of seafood or iodine allergies
options.C: Shave the hair on the patient's abdomen near the umbilicus
options.D: Insert an indwelling urinary catheter for continuous output

explanation: Safety first! Checking for allergies prevents severe reactions to the iodine contrast. You are thinking like a real nurse!

question: Why do health, agriculture, and environment ministries need to work together on food policies?

options.A: It ensures the health ministry controls the whole budget
options.B: It is just a rule required by international banks
options.C: Food production, safety, and nutrition cut across all of these sectors
options.D: It stops farm workers from practicing nursing in clinics

explanation: Solving big food challenges takes teamwork between farming experts, environmentalists, and healthcare professionals!

question: How should a nurse approach a terminally ill patient experiencing deep sadness in the depression stage?

options.A: Request an immediate psychiatric consult for clinical antidepressants
options.B: Distract the patient with busy hospital activities and television
options.C: Encourage the patient to cheer up and focus on positive thoughts
options.D: Provide a quiet, supportive presence and allow expression of grief

explanation: Sadness at this stage is a normal reaction, so offering a comforting presence is more helpful than trying to force artificial cheer. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h5)

question: Where should you place the sticky AED pads on an adult patient's chest?

options.A: Right upper chest and left lower ribcage
options.B: Upper back and lower abdomen
options.C: Directly over the center of the breastbone
options.D: Both shoulders near the outer collarbones

explanation: Placing one pad on the upper right chest and the other on the lower left side creates a diagonal path so the shock travels right through the heart muscle.

question: Why is planning essential for a nursing unit?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for daily staff evaluations
options.B: It prevents chaos and ensures efficient use of resources
options.C: It allows nurses to bypass hospital policies during emergencies
options.D: It ensures that doctors do all the administrative work

explanation: A solid plan helps nurse managers anticipate needs, allocate staff properly, and keep patient care organized and safe. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which drug is a main part of the preferred first-line HIV treatment guidelines in Nigeria?

options.A: Dolutegravir
options.B: Ritonavir
options.C: Zidovudine
options.D: Nevirapine

explanation: Correct! Dolutegravir is a modern, highly effective drug that forms the backbone of standard first-line treatment today.

question: If a vaccine gets ruined by heat, can it be saved by putting it back in the fridge?

options.A: Yes, within twenty-four hours
options.B: Yes, if shaken thoroughly
options.C: No, potency loss is permanent
options.D: Only if it is a viral vaccine

explanation: Once heat damages a vaccine's structure, you can't reverse it. It's always better to discard spoiled doses safely than give an ineffective shot.

question: Which of these common STIs is caused by bacteria and can be easily cured with antibiotics?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.C: Chlamydia
options.D: Herpes simplex virus

explanation: Great job! Chlamydia is bacterial, which means standard antibiotics clear it right up.

question: After giving a subcutaneous injection, which of these details do you NOT need to write in the patient's chart?

options.A: The exact dose and medication given
options.B: The specific site on the body used
options.C: The time and date of administration
options.D: The brand name of the alcohol swab used

explanation: Spot on! You definitely need to log the drug, dose, time, and site, but the brand of your basic prep wipe doesn't matter for clinical records.

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when collecting data for an explanatory study?

options.A: Changing the measurement questions halfway through the study to suit new patients
options.B: Using standardized scales for every single participating subject
options.C: Ensuring tools accurately capture the variables being tested
options.D: Maintaining consistency across all data gathering sessions

explanation: That's right! Changing your questions halfway through ruins your consistency and messes up your findings.

question: What is the primary clinical use of a weighing scale in routine nursing care?

options.A: Assessing nutritional status and tracking fluid balance
options.B: Determining skeletal bone density
options.C: Calculating the total daily calorie intake
options.D: Measuring internal body temperature changes

explanation: Weight measurements help nurses monitor nutritional health and detect sudden fluid shifts in patients. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h1)

question: If a new nursing intervention has a huge standard deviation, which of these is NOT true?

options.A: Every patient in the study experienced a uniform, consistent level of relief
options.B: The overall effectiveness of the treatment varied greatly across the group
options.C: Some patients experienced little to no benefit from the intervention
options.D: Some patients experienced much better results than the average score suggests

explanation: A large standard deviation means results were all over the map—so a uniform, identical result for everyone is definitely incorrect!

question: Why is maintaining the cold chain so important in immunization programs?

options.A: To keep vaccines potent and effective until administration
options.B: To prevent the clinic refrigerator from overheating
options.C: To freeze liquid vaccines into solid blocks
options.D: To make the vaccines easier to draw into a syringe

explanation: Brilliant! Vaccines are delicate biological products. If they get too warm, they lose their power to protect children against diseases.

question: How often should you turn an immobile patient to protect their skin from pressure sores?

options.A: At least every two hours
options.B: Every six hours
options.C: Only when the family asks
options.D: Once every shift

explanation: Turning patients every two hours lets blood flow back into pressed skin, stopping pressure injuries before they start.

question: How is monitoring different from evaluation in a community health project?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.B: Monitoring happens after the project ends, while evaluation happens before
options.C: Monitoring is ongoing review, while evaluation is a periodic impact assessment
options.D: Monitoring focuses only on money, while evaluation focuses only on weather

explanation: Think of monitoring as checking your pulse while running the race, and evaluation as looking at your final race time once you cross the finish line!

question: Why do we need our research questions to be very clear and specific?

options.A: To confuse readers who are not nurses
options.B: To ensure the study collects relevant and measurable data
options.C: To prevent the ethics committee from reading the proposal
options.D: To make the proposal document as long as possible

explanation: Clear questions keep you on track so you don't end up collecting information you don't need!

question: Why is advocacy often necessary alongside health education in community practice?

options.A: Health education is illegal without formal permission from community elders
options.B: Government officials only listen to nurses and ignore the local population
options.C: Advocacy replaces the need to teach people about proper nutrition and hygiene
options.D: Education alone cannot fix environmental and structural problems like lack of clean water

explanation: Even if people know what is healthy, structural barriers like poor infrastructure require political advocacy and community mobilization to fix. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h6)

question: Why is a waste factor or buffer stock added when calculating injection commodities?

options.A: To provide extra income for the hospital pharmacy department
options.B: To ensure the facility has extra funds to pay staff salaries
options.C: To cover dropped items, training breakage, and accidental contamination
options.D: To account for patients who refuse to take their medications

explanation: A buffer percentage ensures unexpected item loss on the ward does not lead to a sudden shortage of clinical tools. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h3)

question: How does severe financial stress usually affect a patient managing a physical disability?

options.A: It ends their need for community support
options.B: It causes immediate bone degeneration
options.C: It makes them less likely to follow their prescribed care plan
options.D: It automatically cures their chronic condition

explanation: When money is tight, patients often have to choose between feeding their families and buying meds or attending follow-up clinics. Financial stress makes adherence very difficult!

question: What is the main reason pregnant women are encouraged to attend routine antenatal care (ANC) visits?

options.A: To provide the mother with high doses of broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: To permanently prevent any potential complications during the postpartum period
options.C: To schedule the exact date and time when labor will officially begin
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for conditions like anemia and high blood pressure

explanation: ANC is like a check-point for safety! It helps midwives and nurses catch small issues like low blood levels or high BP early before they become emergencies.

question: Which healthcare professional should you team up with when a patient has trouble chewing or swallowing?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Hospital administrative clerk
options.C: Physical rehabilitation trainer
options.D: Biochemical laboratory technician

explanation: Speech therapists are experts at assessing swallowing disorders and helping patients eat safely. Teamwork makes the dream work!

question: A persistently high maternal mortality ratio in a specific region most strongly points to which underlying issue?

options.A: A cultural preference for giving birth during the rainy season
options.B: Weaknesses or failures within the local emergency healthcare system
options.C: An unusually high rate of twin and triplet births in the community
options.D: Excessive availability of free antenatal care medications

explanation: When maternal mortality stays high, it usually points to poor access to skilled birth attendants, delayed referrals, and inadequate emergency care. Recognizing this helps us know where to fix the system!

question: Why might a single medication belong to more than one distinct category?

options.A: Because it can be classified by its chemical structure or disease treated
options.B: Because doctors use random methods to sort medications
options.C: Because drug companies change the name of the drug every year
options.D: Because government laws require multiple names for safety

explanation: A drug can be sorted differently based on how it is made, how it acts in the body, or the specific illness it targets. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why do we view disaster management as an endless cycle rather than a straight line?

options.A: Because recovery takes the exact same amount of time as mitigation
options.B: Because lessons learned during recovery directly inform future mitigation and preparedness
options.C: Because disasters always happen at the exact same time every year
options.D: Because emergency personnel never stop responding to disasters

explanation: Brilliant! Every time we recover from a disaster, we learn valuable lessons that help us get better prepared for the next one.

question: What is the internationally accepted age below which any marriage is classified as an early or child marriage?

options.A: Under 18 years of age
options.B: Under 15 years of age
options.C: Under 16 years of age
options.D: Under 21 years of age

explanation: Great job! Global health standards consider anyone under 18 a minor. Any union below this age is classed as early marriage, no matter local customs.

question: When a patient with a throat infection develops a high fever, tiredness, and swollen neck glands, what do these show?

options.A: Lower airway collapse
options.B: Systemic response to the infection
options.C: Permanent vocal cord damage
options.D: Localized allergic rhinitis

explanation: Spot on! Fever and swollen lymph glands are signs that the whole body's immune system is active and fighting the germs.

question: A patient has a deep pressure ulcer on their heel that is draining a lot of fluid. Which dressing is best to handle it?

options.A: Transparent film
options.B: Dry cotton gauze
options.C: Foam dressing
options.D: Paper tape

explanation: Foam dressings are fantastic at cushioning fragile skin while soaking up moderate-to-heavy drainage. Spot on!

question: Why do many patients find it hard to stick to a low-sodium diet at first?

options.A: Fresh vegetables completely lose all their nutritional value
options.B: Taste buds take time to adjust, making food taste bland initially
options.C: The human brain loses the ability to feel thirsty
options.D: Low-sodium foods are chemically impossible for the stomach to digest

explanation: Exactly! Our taste buds need a little patience to readjust to less salt, but once they do, natural food flavors start shining through!

question: Which specific brain receptors do central anticholinergics block?

options.A: Opioid receptors
options.B: Adrenergic receptors
options.C: Nicotinic receptors
options.D: Muscarinic receptors

explanation: Central anticholinergics target and block muscarinic receptors to reduce cholinergic activity. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h2)

question: Why are straps fastened across the chest, hips, and knees during ambulance transport?

options.A: To increase blood flow directly back to the heart chambers
options.B: To stop the patient from talking too loudly to the driver
options.C: To keep the patient completely awake throughout the journey
options.D: To prevent the patient from sliding or falling during sharp turns

explanation: Ambulances make sudden turns and stops, making secure strapping vital to keep the patient safe on the stretcher. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the main difference between curative treatment and palliative care?

options.A: Curative treatment aims to eradicate disease, while palliative care focuses on comfort and quality of life.
options.B: Curative treatment is only for the elderly, while palliative care is for young children.
options.C: Curative treatment ignores physical pain, while palliative care focuses only on surgery.
options.D: Curative treatment is provided at home, while palliative care requires an intensive care unit.

explanation: Think of it this way: curative treatment fights the disease itself to get rid of it, while palliative care fights the discomfort and pain so the patient can feel better day-to-day. You've got this!

question: Why was the Minimum Data Set (MDS) introduced as part of the 1987 reforms?

options.A: To determine which staff members should be terminated each quarter
options.B: To standardize comprehensive resident assessments and guide individualized care planning
options.C: To calculate the exact profit margins for private facility owners
options.D: To track how many visitors each resident received every week

explanation: The MDS is a fantastic tool for nurses! It ensures every resident gets a thorough health assessment so the team can build a care plan tailored specifically to that person's needs.

question: What major postpartum emergency is an anaemic woman most at risk for?

options.A: Sudden closing of her airway
options.B: Sudden buildup of amniotic fluid
options.C: Hypovolemic shock from normal blood loss
options.D: Temporary leg paralysis

explanation: Since her blood reserves are already low, losing even a standard amount of blood after birth can push her straight into shock.

question: Why does regular physical activity keep our muscles healthy and strong?

options.A: It removes the need for dietary protein intake
options.B: It permanently increases the total number of muscle fibers
options.C: It maintains muscle protein synthesis and strength
options.D: It completely stops the normal aging process of bones

explanation: You've got this! Active muscle use stimulates protein building blocks and metabolic processes, keeping muscle fibers strong and preventing wasting.

question: What is the main use of the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) in the ward?

options.A: To test the patient's long-term memory
options.B: To diagnose the exact cause of a brain injury
options.C: To check the strength of peripheral nerves
options.D: To measure a patient's level of consciousness

explanation: You'll use the GCS every day on clinical placement! It gives us a quick, reliable way to check and record how alert a patient is. You've got this!

question: Which of these crops make up the traditional, local staple foods in Nigerian diets?

options.A: Imported canned beef and biscuits
options.B: Yams, millet, and sorghum
options.C: Processed wheat and refined sugar
options.D: Temperate climate root vegetables

explanation: Spot on! Traditional Nigerian diets rely heavily on locally grown grains, tubers, and legumes that thrive right here in our climate.

question: What is the ultimate goal of patient education when teaching someone how to care for their diabetes at home?

options.A: Preventing the patient from ever experiencing normal life stress
options.B: Eliminating all future visits to the primary healthcare clinic
options.C: Empowering the patient to safely manage their daily condition
options.D: Ensuring the family takes complete control of medication administration

explanation: Good education gives patients the tools, knowledge, and confidence to take charge of their own health every day. Love to see it!

question: What does professional autonomy mean for a modern clinical nurse?

options.A: Working completely isolated from doctors and laboratory scientists
options.B: Making independent, accountable clinical decisions within one's scope of practice
options.C: Refusing to follow hospital administrative policies or protocols
options.D: Prescribing major pharmaceutical drugs without medical supervision

explanation: Exactly! Autonomy means having the confidence and professional right to make sound clinical choices within your training limits.

question: Which of the following is a common challenge for tele-nursing practice in developing regions?

options.A: Erratic electricity supply and poor internet connectivity
options.B: Patients refusing to use phones for any medical reason
options.C: An overabundance of advanced video monitoring equipment
options.D: Excessive physical contact between nurses and clients

explanation: Unreliable power and weak network signals frequently interrupt remote healthcare delivery in resource-constrained settings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h5)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of acute salpingitis?

options.A: Sharp pain located exclusively in the upper right shoulder
options.B: Bilateral lower abdominal and pelvic pain
options.C: Severe itching of the external perineal skin
options.D: Painless swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: Since both tubes can be affected, inflammation usually shows up as lower belly or pelvic pain felt on both sides.

question: How can a lower GNP indirectly lead to poorer health outcomes in a community?

options.A: By automatically increasing the number of trained nurses in rural posts
options.B: By eliminating the need for primary healthcare facilities
options.C: By limiting access to basic sanitation, clean water, and nutrition
options.D: By directly mutating viral strains in local communities

explanation: When money is tight nationally, basic needs like clean water and good food become harder for families to access, leading to more sickness. It's a tough reality, but understanding it helps us advocate for our patients!

question: A nurse notices a sudden cluster of patients arriving with severe vomiting and diarrhea from the same neighborhood. What action best reflects hazard identification?

options.A: Asking the hospital finance department to buy more IV fluids
options.B: Waiting until next week to see if more people show up at the clinic
options.C: Reporting the unusual disease pattern to public health authorities immediately
options.D: Telling the patients it is just a normal stomach flu and sending them home

explanation: Spotting unusual symptom clusters and alerting authorities helps catch outbreaks early before they turn into major disasters. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why is two-way communication so important in IEC strategies?

options.A: It allows healthcare providers to address community doubts and fears directly
options.B: It forces community members to strictly follow doctor orders without questions
options.C: It replaces the need for medical treatments during community outreaches
options.D: It ensures that patients never have to visit the hospital for care

explanation: Communication isn't just about giving orders! A good chat lets us listen to people's worries and build real trust. You've got this!

question: What are the three components of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Vector, vaccine, and immunity
options.B: Agent, host, and environment
options.C: Bacteria, virus, and fungus
options.D: Primary, secondary, and tertiary

explanation: The classic epidemiological model uses the agent, host, and environment to explain how diseases are transmitted. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary digestive function of the oral cavity?

options.A: Absorption of complex carbohydrates into the bloodstream
options.B: Production of powerful hydrochloric acid to sterilize food
options.C: Complete enzymatic breakdown and absorption of proteins
options.D: Mechanical breakdown of food and mixing it with saliva

explanation: The mouth starts digestion by chewing food into smaller pieces and mixing it with saliva to create an easy-to-swallow bolus. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h1)

question: You see a sudden, sharp spike on a monthly infection rate graph that is normally very flat. What should you suspect first?

options.A: The normal daily fluctuation of a healthy patient
options.B: An isolated event, outbreak, or possible data recording error
options.C: A permanent and irreversible change in hospital policy
options.D: The complete eradication of the infectious disease

explanation: Spot on! Sudden peaks jump out because they don't fit the normal pattern—usually pointing to an outbreak or a quick typo in the log.

question: In the theatre team, who is mainly responsible for writing down the counts on the whiteboard?

options.A: The lead surgeon
options.B: The scrub nurse
options.C: The anesthetist
options.D: The circulating nurse

explanation: The circulating nurse is outside the sterile field (unsterile zone), which makes them the perfect person to maintain the official tally board.

question: Why is it vital for hospitals to offer structured support programs for healthcare providers after adverse events?

options.A: To trick staff into admitting legal guilt so the hospital can fire them easily
options.B: To help clinicians process trauma and prevent long-term burnout or leaving the profession
options.C: To replace the need for conducting an actual Root Cause Analysis
options.D: To distract the public from noticing that a mistake occurred

explanation: Support programs protect staff well-being, helping them recover emotionally and continue providing safe care. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h7)

question: A toddler is showing growth faltering. What is the most practical nutrition advice to give the mother?

options.A: Stop all breastfeeding immediately and switch entirely to cow milk
options.B: Only feed the child imported baby cereals bought from supermarkets
options.C: Reduce the number of daily meals to allow the child's stomach to rest
options.D: Use available local food items to make nutrient-dense meals given more frequently

explanation: Keep advice practical! Recommend affordable, locally available foods that the family can easily prepare and feed the child more often.

question: How does filtered bicarbonate cross the cell membrane of the kidney tubule?

options.A: It attaches to carrier proteins designed for glucose transport
options.B: It passes directly through large protein channels in the membrane
options.C: It converts to carbon dioxide and water before crossing
options.D: It is actively pumped across by specialized sodium carriers

explanation: Bicarbonate can't easily cross the membrane on its own because of its charge. So, it cleverly teams up with hydrogen to form gas and water first, which easily slip across!

question: A patient discharged after treatment for nephrotic syndrome calls the clinic reporting a new, warm, swollen, and painful calf. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Normal muscle recovery after being on bed rest
options.B: An allergic reaction to the prescribed diuretic
options.C: Rapid healing of the kidney filtration barrier
options.D: A deep vein thrombosis due to protein loss

explanation: Unilateral calf pain and swelling in a patient with nephrotic syndrome is a classic red flag for a deep vein thrombosis caused by altered clotting factors. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h7)

question: What makes an infectious substance fit into Category A instead of Category B?

options.A: It can cause fatal or life-threatening disease upon exposure
options.B: It is shipped in much larger liquid volumes than normal samples
options.C: It only affects animals and never poses any risk to human health
options.D: It consists solely of routine urine and stool sample containers

explanation: Category A is for the scary, high-risk stuff that can cause severe or fatal illness, so it needs extra-tough packaging. Excellent practice for clinical safety!

question: A new mother bleeds heavily because a small piece of the placenta was left behind in the uterus. Which of the 4 Ts does this fall under?

options.A: Thrombin
options.B: Tone
options.C: Trauma
options.D: Tissue

explanation: When membranes or pieces of the placenta stay behind inside, we group that under 'Tissue'. Making sure the placenta is complete upon delivery prevents this!

question: Why is leaving an EMR workstation logged in and walk away a big professional risk?

options.A: Hospital management will automatically dock your monthly salary
options.B: Patients will be able to alter their own discharge instructions
options.C: Anyone can document care under your name, making you legally responsible
options.D: The computer screen saver will permanently burn out from inactivity

explanation: Always lock your screen! Because entries are tied to your specific login, you take the blame for anything done on that open terminal.

question: What do we call it when liquid soaks through a sterile drape, drawing bacteria up from the unsterile surface underneath?

options.A: Surface sterilization failure
options.B: Strike-through contamination
options.C: Capillary flow breach
options.D: Airborne droplet transfer

explanation: Moisture creates a bridge for germs to travel through tiny holes in drapes. That's why keeping sterile fields dry is so important!

question: As a nurse preparing a discharge plan for a patient recovering from an incomplete abortion, which action directly fulfills the family planning pillar of PAC?

options.A: Discussing and providing the client's preferred modern contraceptive method
options.B: Scheduling a mandatory follow-up appointment for major pelvic surgery
options.C: Handing out educational pamphlets on infant nutrition and immunization
options.D: Referral to social welfare for financial empowerment programs

explanation: Well done! Providing contraceptive services before discharge helps women prevent future unintended pregnancies.

question: Why are OR electrical outlets hooked up to emergency backup generators?

options.A: To provide power for the cleaning staff's vacuum cleaners
options.B: To lower the monthly electricity bill for the hospital
options.C: To prevent life-support and monitoring equipment from shutting down during power failures
options.D: To allow staff to charge personal mobile phones safely

explanation: You nailed it! Power failure in Nigeria or anywhere else shouldn't stop life-support monitors or surgical machines mid-operation.

question: When cleaning a hospital ward, why should you always clean from high areas to low areas, and clean zones to dirty zones?

options.A: To ensure that heavy cleaning buckets stay balanced on wheeled carts
options.B: To prevent dirt and pathogens from falling onto already cleaned surfaces
options.C: To reduce the total amount of chemical spray needed for the room
options.D: To speed up the chemical evaporation rate across large ward floors

explanation: Working top-to-bottom stops gravity from dropping dust and germs right back onto the spots you just finished cleaning!

question: Which questionnaire is widely used to check different parts of female sexual function?

options.A: Mini-Mental State Examination
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Beck Depression Inventory
options.D: Female Sexual Function Index

explanation: You got it! The FSFI is the go-to tool researchers and clinicians use to measure things like desire, arousal, and comfort.

question: Which type of vaccine uses a weakened live germ to give long-lasting immunity, often with just a few doses?

options.A: Inactivated
options.B: Subunit
options.C: Live-attenuated
options.D: Toxoid

explanation: Live-attenuated vaccines act like a mild natural infection, training your immune cells really well so they remember the germ for a long time.

question: What is the main job of the vital centres in your body?

options.A: Processing conscious thoughts and logic
options.B: Storing long-term memories and emotions
options.C: Controlling voluntary muscle movements
options.D: Managing basic life-sustaining functions automatically

explanation: You don't have to think about breathing or your heart beating! Vital centres run these automatic survival tasks behind the scenes.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to respond when a client shares a traditional belief that goes against medical science?

options.A: Argue aggressively until the client agrees to abandon their tradition
options.B: Scold the client publicly to discourage others from holding similar views
options.C: Listen patiently and gently provide accurate health education without mockery
options.D: Ignore the client and refuse to provide any further medical care

explanation: Spot on! Respectful listening builds trust, making the client much more willing to listen to your advice.

question: A public health nurse is tracking down everyone who spent time near a patient with an active bacterial infection. What is this nursing action called?

options.A: Vector control
options.B: Environmental sterilization
options.C: Active immunization
options.D: Contact tracing

explanation: Brilliant! This is a core public health nursing duty. Tracing contacts helps us find everyone who might have caught the bug and stops the transmission chain right in its tracks.

question: What is a common brain-related sign of inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Immediate normalization of deep tendon reflexes
options.B: Rapid regeneration of damaged nerve fibers
options.C: Sudden and permanent recovery of lost motor skills
options.D: Progressive cognitive decline and memory loss

explanation: As neural pathways break down step by step, patients sadly experience a steady drop in memory and thinking skills.

question: A patient receiving an anti-bleeding drug suddenly gets short of breath and has chest pain. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: An acute iron deficiency
options.B: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: A mild kidney infection
options.D: A pulmonary embolism

question: Why might a vaccine that works brilliantly in a research lab fail to protect a community completely in real life?

options.A: Microorganisms in the community mutate faster than laboratory strains
options.B: Real-world storage issues and varied human health statuses reduce its impact
options.C: Laboratory tests use synthetic antigens that behave differently than real viruses
options.D: Clinical trials always overestimate the dosage required for human immunity

explanation: Labs are controlled, but the real world has fridge power cuts and different individual health states. It's a great reminder of why public health nursing is so dynamic!

question: What is the main goal of infant welfare clinics in primary healthcare?

options.A: To manufacture and distribute infant formula milk
options.B: To reduce infant illness and death through prevention
options.C: To provide long-term inpatient admission for babies
options.D: To treat severe surgical emergencies in newborns

explanation: Spot on! Infant welfare clinics are all about stopping sickness before it starts through immunizations, health talks, and early check-ups.

question: When giving perineal care, in which direction should you wash to prevent spreading germs?

options.C: In a circular motion starting from the outer thighs inward

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should tell a patient being treated for infectious cervicitis?

question: What is a major reason why unsafe injections happen in low-resource clinics?

options.A: Having too many nurses on duty at night
options.B: Having way too many sterile water supplies
options.C: Shortages of disposable syringes and safety boxes
options.D: Too many mandatory infection control classes

explanation: When basic supplies run low, healthcare workers are put in tough spots. Advocating for proper supplies is a big part of nursing advocacy.

question: Why can it be so tricky to spot a drug side effect in someone with a degenerative disease?

options.A: Patients with degenerative illnesses never tell anyone how they feel
options.B: Lab tests can never detect drug levels in chronic illnesses
options.C: Drug side effects always cause a sudden skin rash
options.D: Side effects like tremors or confusion can easily look like the disease getting worse

question: Why do proton pumps in the collecting duct rely on primary active transport?

options.A: To push hydrogen ions against a very steep concentration gradient
options.B: To reabsorb all filtered glucose before it reaches the bladder
options.C: To prevent potassium from entering the urine under normal conditions

question: Why is community health education so crucial for fighting cancer in Nigeria?

options.A: It replaces the need for palliative nurses
options.B: It guarantees free surgeries at every health post
options.C: It helps clear up harmful myths and encourages early hospital visits
options.D: It completely stops genetic mutations from happening

explanation: When we educate our communities with love and facts, we break down fear and cultural barriers so people seek help early. You are going to make a great nurse!

question: Which of these does NOT cause an error when using an infrared thermometer?

options.A: Bringing the device straight from a cold room into a warm ward
options.B: Using a brand new disposable probe cover
options.C: Heavy sweat on the patient's forehead
options.D: Accumulated earwax in the ear canal

explanation: A clean probe cover is what you *want* to use! It keeps things hygienic and won't mess up your reading.

question: Why are older adults much more likely to experience bad side effects from medications?

options.A: They always forget to swallow their pills with water
options.B: Their stomach acid completely destroys all medications
options.C: Their bodies metabolize and excrete medications much slower
options.D: They prefer taking herbal remedies instead of real drugs

explanation: Because liver and kidney functions slow down with age, drugs hang around in the body much longer. If doses aren't adjusted, they can easily build up to toxic levels.

question: How does carrying extra body weight lead to osteoarthritis in weight-bearing joints?

options.A: By increasing bone density beyond normal limits
options.B: By blocking blood flow to the synovial lining
options.C: By adding mechanical stress and releasing inflammatory fat proteins
options.D: By causing sudden bacterial infections in the joint capsule

explanation: Extra weight acts like a heavy physical load on knees and hips, while fat tissue also pumps out inflammatory proteins that break down cartilage faster.

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients dealing with amenorrhoea?

options.A: Emotional support replaces the need for any complex diagnostic blood testing
options.B: Patients will refuse all physical examinations unless their anxiety is treated first
options.C: Psychological stress is the only scientifically proven cause of primary amenorrhoea
options.D: Changes in menstrual patterns often create strong emotional distress regarding identity and fertility

explanation: Not seeing a regular period can be really scary for a young woman, often triggering worries about her womanhood and future family.

question: A patient has a high fever and flushed, warm skin. Which process is the body using to cool down?

options.A: Vasoconstriction and shivering
options.B: Vasodilation and sweating
options.C: Keratin buildup and cell shedding
options.D: Fat storage and hair growth

question: What is a major perk of practicing procedures on advanced robotic manikins?

options.A: They grade your care plans automatically so instructors don't have to
options.B: You can practice emergencies safely without putting real patients at risk
options.C: They don't need any electricity or upkeep to work
options.D: They completely replace going to the hospital for clinicals

explanation: Simulators let you make mistakes and fix them on a dummy first, building your confidence before you care for a living person.

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe condition for a home delivery?

options.A: Singleton pregnancy
options.B: Head-down baby position
options.C: Normal blood pressure
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: Placenta previa causes severe bleeding and requires immediate hospital management, making home delivery extremely dangerous. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h4)

question: How does narrowing the skin's blood vessels help protect you in a cold environment?

options.A: By increasing sweat production to insulate the epidermis
options.B: By forcing the skeletal muscles to relax completely
options.C: By speeding up evaporation from the skin surface
options.D: By keeping warm blood near the core and away from the skin

question: What is the main job of the alveoli in the breast?

options.A: Storing fat to give the breast shape
options.B: Synthesizing and secreting milk
options.C: Producing oxytocin for uterine contractions
options.D: Transporting milk directly to the skin surface

question: What is the final, main product of the process of oogenesis?

options.A: A fertilized zygote
options.B: An immature polar body
options.C: A mature haploid ovum
options.D: A diploid spermatogonium

explanation: Great start! Oogenesis is simply how female eggs (ova) are formed, resulting in a mature haploid ovum that is ready for fertilization.

question: Which lab result strongly suggests that a bile duct is blocked?

options.A: Decreased serum potassium levels
options.B: Low white blood cell count
options.C: Elevated serum bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
options.D: Increased red blood cell mass

question: How do pests like rats and flies make unmanaged hospital rubbish so dangerous?

options.A: They physically carry pathogens from the waste back into living and treatment areas
options.B: They consume all the toxic chemicals and render the waste completely harmless
options.C: They increase the rate at which biodegradable plastics break down in the sun
options.D: They serve as reliable biological indicators for routine environmental audits

question: In maritime healthcare, what does the abbreviation TMAS stand for?

options.A: Transport Medical Action System
options.B: Trauma Management At Sea
options.C: Total Maritime Air Support
options.D: Telemedical Assistance Service

explanation: You got it! TMAS connects ships at sea with land-based medical experts for remote guidance and advice.

question: How does great teamwork between doctors, nurses, and pharmacists improve safety?

options.A: By ensuring all team members share critical concerns and catch dosing errors early
options.B: By reducing the total number of medications any patient is allowed to take
options.C: By allowing nurses to bypass doctors and prescribe medications independently
options.D: By shifting all legal responsibility for medication errors onto the pharmacist

explanation: Open communication builds a safety net around the patient. When we talk to each other, mistakes get caught early!

question: In which part of the prostate gland does benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) usually start?

options.A: Transition zone
options.B: Seminal vesicle
options.C: Central zone
options.D: Peripheral zone

question: Why do our hands and face get a much larger area on the sensory homunculus than our back or thighs?

options.A: They are closer physically to the brain

options.C: They receive more blood flow from the carotid arteries
