question: What are the two main jobs of the external male reproductive organs?

options.A: Hormone production and digestion
options.B: Sperm maturation and temperature regulation
options.C: Blood filtration and fluid balance
options.D: Urine elimination and sexual reproduction

explanation: You've got it! The penis and urethra pull double duty: they help pass out urine from the bladder and also help deliver sperm during reproduction.

question: Why is calming a patient's emotions just as important as treating their physical wounds in a crisis?

options.A: It completely erases the memory of the traumatic event
options.B: It speeds up the hospital discharge process for all patients
options.C: It prevents the physical injuries from becoming infected
options.D: It lowers acute stress and supports physical healing

explanation: Great thinking! When we help patients calm down, their stress hormones drop, making it much easier for their bodies to heal and for them to work with us.

question: Why is putting a child in an orphanage usually considered a last resort?

options.A: Extended family members refuse to let children visit orphanages
options.B: Family-based care is better for a child's emotional development
options.C: Orphanages are illegal under Nigerian federal health laws
options.D: Institutions only accept children who are over eighteen years old

explanation: Children always thrive better emotionally and socially when raised within a family setting rather than an institution. Family love is powerful medicine!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical sign of an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction?

options.A: Fever and severe lower back pain
options.B: Sudden drop in body temperature and shivering
options.C: Chest tightness and feeling of impending doom
options.D: Dark-colored urine caused by free hemoglobin

explanation: Watch out for trick questions like this! Transfusion reactions usually cause a fever, not a drop in temperature, along with back pain, dark urine, and anxiety. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h6)

question: What does the term 'countertransference' mean in nursing?

options.A: When the hospital administration changes a patient's care assignment
options.B: When the nurse projects personal feelings or unresolved issues onto the patient
options.C: When the patient projects feelings from past relationships onto the nurse
options.D: When communication breaks down due to language and cultural barriers

explanation: Countertransference happens when you accidentally let your own personal emotions, memories, or biases spill over onto how you treat a patient.

question: According to the healthy plate method, what portion of a meal should be fruits and vegetables?

options.A: The entire plate
options.B: One-quarter
options.C: Three-quarters
options.D: One-half

explanation: Filling half the plate with colorful fruits and veggies is a quick, easy rule to make sure a meal is full of fiber and vitamins.

question: A patient wanting a medical abortion has an IUD in place. What should the nurse make sure happens first?

options.A: Ensure the IUD is removed prior to starting the misoprostol regimen
options.B: Leave the IUD in because misoprostol will push it out
options.C: Give extra antibiotics to stop local infections
options.D: Switch the patient immediately to vacuum aspiration

explanation: We need to take out any IUD before starting treatment to prevent serious infections or heavy bleeding. Simple and important safety step!

question: Which waste product builds up in the blood to cause hepatic encephalopathy?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Ammonia
options.D: Sodium

explanation: A healthy liver turns nitrogen waste like ammonia into safe urea. When the liver fails, ammonia builds up and affects brain function, causing confusion.

question: Why is tetanus considered infectious, but not strictly communicable?

options.A: It spreads through the air rather than direct contact.
options.B: It cannot be treated with any known medications.
options.C: It only affects animals and never human beings.
options.D: It enters the body from the environment and does not spread from person to person.

explanation: Think of it this way: tetanus spores live in the soil and get in through wounds. You cannot catch tetanus directly from a patient lying next to you in the ward!

question: What is the main goal of teaching a family home care after treating a patient for head lice?

options.A: To prove that the nursing staff performed their duties correctly
options.B: To prevent reinfection and spread among household members
options.C: To force the family to cut their hair short for safety
options.D: To ensure the patient buys the most expensive commercial products

explanation: Good teaching helps families clean bedding and check everyone else, stopping the lice from spreading right back to the patient! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: A nurse tests a new pain medication and measures the patient's reported pain score. What represents the independent variable?

options.A: The reported pain score
options.B: The new pain medication
options.C: The patient's age
options.D: The hospital noise level

explanation: The medication is what the researcher changes or gives to the patient, making it the independent variable (the cause). [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h4)

question: The AED just delivered a shock to your patient. What is the very next thing your team should do?

options.A: Resume high-quality chest compressions immediately
options.B: Remove the AED pads and prepare to transport the patient
options.C: Wait for the device to automatically perform a second analysis
options.D: Check the carotid artery for a strong pulse for one minute

explanation: Don't wait! Right after a shock, jump straight back into chest compressions. Let the AED guide you when it's time for the next rhythm check.

question: What is the primary focus of preventive nursing in musculoskeletal health?

options.A: Surgical repair of broken bones
options.B: Prescribing strong pain medications
options.C: Stopping injuries before they happen
options.D: Treating chronic joint infections

explanation: Preventive nursing aims to identify risks and educate patients to stop musculoskeletal problems before they develop. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h1)

question: Why were early almshouses poorly suited for caring for the sick and elderly?

options.A: They suffered from severe overcrowding and a lack of medical staff
options.B: They charged fees that only wealthy families could afford
options.C: They focused too heavily on expensive experimental therapies
options.D: They refused to admit anyone over the age of fifty

explanation: These places were often jam-packed and lacked trained health workers. Mixing different vulnerable people together without proper medical care meant chronic illnesses weren't managed well.

question: What is the primary hormone responsible for moving glucose from the bloodstream into body cells?

options.A: Cortisol
options.B: Amylase
options.C: Glucagon
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Insulin acts as a cellular key that allows circulating glucose to enter body tissues for energy use. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h1)

question: What is a likely result when nurses on a ward lack motivation?

options.A: Increased risk of clinical errors and high staff turnover
options.B: Better compliance with mandatory documentation standards
options.C: Decreased utilization of hospital supply inventories
options.D: Faster recovery times for postoperative surgical patients

explanation: When the team is burned out and unmotivated, mistakes happen more easily, and nurses tend to leave. Keeping morale up keeps patients safer!

question: Why do the testes hang outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To allow rapid absorption of testosterone directly into the skin
options.B: To keep the testicles cooler than body temperature for sperm production
options.C: To provide a direct connection to the external urinary meatus
options.D: To protect the reproductive organs from high intra-abdominal pressure

explanation: Sperm are sensitive! They need a slightly cooler temperature than the rest of the body to grow and develop properly, which is why the scrotum hangs outside.

question: Why is a speech therapist often called in to help patients with advanced neurodegenerative disorders?

options.A: To teach them foreign languages
options.B: To cure their underlying memory loss
options.C: To help manage swallowing and communication issues
options.D: To improve their walking balance and posture

explanation: Speech therapists do more than just speech—they train and protect the muscles used for swallowing, which stops dangerous choking and aspiration. Fantastic nursing awareness!

question: How do changing body shapes during pregnancy typically affect a woman's body image?

options.A: They invariably cause permanent clinical body dysmorphia
options.B: They produce mixed responses ranging from empowerment to distress
options.C: They have zero emotional impact on the expectant mother
options.D: They universally improve self-esteem across all trimesters

explanation: Every woman is different! Some love their glowing bump while others struggle with the physical changes, and both reactions are valid.

question: Why is objective documentation of health education important for the community health team?

options.A: It guarantees that the client will follow their treatment plan perfectly
options.B: It replaces the need for face-to-face conversations with families
options.C: It prevents clients from ever asking follow-up questions
options.D: It ensures continuity of care so other nurses know what was taught

explanation: Clear notes allow different healthcare providers to see what education has already been provided, maintaining consistency in ongoing care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h8)

question: What is the most common opportunistic infection and leading cause of death in people with HIV?

options.A: Tetanus
options.B: Tuberculosis
options.C: Cholera
options.D: Malaria

explanation: Tuberculosis (TB) is the top opportunistic infection we watch out for in patients with weakened immune systems. Catching it early saves lives!

question: A patient's chest tube accidentally falls completely out of their chest. What should you do immediately?

options.A: Leave the open chest wound completely uncovered and run to find a doctor
options.B: Put clean gloves on and push the exact same tube back into the chest wound
options.C: Clamp the remaining chest tubing tightly to preserve negative pressure
options.D: Cover the site with a sterile petroleum dressing taped on three sides

explanation: A three-sided petroleum dressing acts like a smart flap—it lets trapped air escape while stopping room air from sucking back in.

question: Prolonged pressure from the baby's head against the bladder during difficult labour can lead to which lasting complication?

options.A: Gestational hypertension
options.B: Vesicovaginal fistula
options.C: Chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: This is a key one in midwifery practice. Continuous pressure cuts off blood flow to the bladder wall, forming an opening (fistula) that causes constant urine leakage.

question: Which part of the brain acts as the body's natural thermostat during a fever?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Hypothalamus
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The hypothalamus is like the internal thermostat in your brain. It turns up the heat when your body needs to fight off an infection.

question: When calculating an incidence rate, what goes into the denominator (the bottom number)?

options.A: The total number of deaths recorded in the hospital
options.B: The total budget allocated for public health programs
options.C: The number of patients who have already recovered
options.D: The total population at risk of getting the disease

explanation: When calculating rates, your denominator must only include people who can actually catch the disease. Makes complete sense when you think about it!

question: A baby is born at 36 weeks with clear fluid, but has weak muscle tone and is gasping for air. What is your immediate next step?

options.A: Move the baby to the warmer for initial steps
options.B: Immediately start chest compressions and epinephrine
options.C: Administer rescue breaths using a bag-valve-mask
options.D: Leave the baby with the mother for skin-to-skin care

explanation: Poor tone and gasping mean the baby needs extra help right away. Take them to the radiant warmer to clear their airway and help them breathe.

question: What is the primary goal of government food safety regulations?

options.A: To increase the cost of importing foreign goods
options.B: To prevent foodborne illnesses and contamination
options.C: To make sure all food items taste identical
options.D: To prevent small vendors from selling fresh produce

explanation: Safety regulations protect consumers from harmful biological and chemical agents found in unsafe food. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h4)

question: What is the medical term when a baby is born without a fallopian tube?

options.A: Ovarian hypoplasia
options.B: Tubal agenesis
options.C: Uterine didelphys
options.D: Cervical stenosis

explanation: You've got this! 'Tubal agenesis' simply means the fallopian tube didn't form during development before birth. It's a great term to tuck away in your nursing notes.

question: Due to physical immaturity, which medical complication is especially common in pregnant adolescents?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.B: Primary pulmonary hypertension
options.C: Chronic autoimmune thyroiditis
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Spot on! Young mothers face a higher risk of developing pregnancy-induced hypertension and preeclampsia compared to older women.

question: Why do you hold the first removed glove inside the palm of your remaining gloved hand?

options.A: To stop the latex from releasing powder into the air
options.B: To easily peel off the second glove without touching its dirty outside
options.C: To keep the first glove clean so you can use it again
options.D: To save space in the waste bin

explanation: Ball up the first glove in your palm so your bare fingers can safely slide under the clean inner cuff of the second glove. Clever and safe!

question: Why are system-level changes much better than simply telling staff to 'be more careful'?

options.A: Staff members refuse to listen to verbal warnings from managers
options.B: Hospital administration prefers buying new equipment over training
options.C: Training sessions take too much time away from patient care duties
options.D: Human beings are fallible and will always make mistakes under stress

explanation: Spot on! Relying solely on human vigilance fails because everyone gets tired and stressed. Good systems protect both the nurse and the patient!

question: Why must you let the skin antiseptic dry completely before starting an IV stick?

options.A: To allow the chemical to fully destroy microorganisms on the skin
options.B: To ensure the vein stays plump and easy to palpate
options.C: To prevent the sticky dressing from sliding off wet skin
options.D: To stop the client from feeling a sharp burning sensation

explanation: Patience pays off! Antiseptics like chlorhexidine need a little contact and drying time to actually kill the germs on the skin before you puncture it.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge for monitoring and evaluation in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Inconsistent electricity and poor internet connectivity
options.B: Staff shortages and heavy workloads for nurses
options.C: Fatigue from filling out multiple paper registers
options.D: Unlimited budgets and an excess of electronic tablets

explanation: Resource-limited settings are known for budget constraints and shortages, so having unlimited funds and excess tablets is definitely not the norm!

question: Which action truly shows compassionate end-of-life nursing care for a dying patient at home?

options.A: Limiting family visits to ensure quiet hospital-like rules
options.B: Encouraging the patient to walk outside despite extreme weakness
options.C: Focusing strictly on lab test results and vital signs
options.D: Supporting family members and managing the patient's pain effectively

explanation: You got it! End-of-life nursing is all about easing physical pain and offering a warm, supportive shoulder to both the patient and their loved ones.

question: Your heart beats and your food digests automatically without you having to think about it. Which system runs this show?

options.A: Cerebellar motor system
options.B: Central reflex system
options.C: Somatic nervous system
options.D: Autonomic nervous system

explanation: The autonomic system runs automatically in the background so you can focus on your nursing notes. Well done! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is a major ethical debate surrounding Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) like IVF?

options.A: Guaranteed elimination of all genetic diseases at birth
options.B: Compulsory fertility treatment for all citizens
options.C: Fair access and what to do with unused embryos
options.D: Total absence of any legal regulations worldwide

explanation: ART often raises tough questions about fairness in who can afford it and how leftover embryos should be handled ethically. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h6)

question: What do the ciliary muscles do when you switch from looking at a distant wall to reading a book close to your face?

options.A: They pull the iris wide open
options.B: They contract to make the lens thicker
options.C: They relax to make the lens thinner
options.D: They push the cornea outward

explanation: For close-up reading, your ciliary muscles tighten up, letting the lens get nice and round to focus clearly. You're doing great!

question: What does population health nursing primarily focus on?

options.A: The financial balance sheet of a health clinic
options.B: The health outcomes of an entire group of people
options.C: The surgical procedures performed in a single hospital ward
options.D: The genetic profile of an individual patient

explanation: Population health looks beyond the individual patient to protect and promote the well-being of whole communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of emotional distress in a patient?

options.A: Sudden and severe social withdrawal
options.B: Persistent sadness and frequent crying
options.C: Expressing feelings of total hopelessness
options.D: Steady weight gain and cheerful laughter

explanation: Laughter and a steady weight are generally positive signs! Crying, hopelessness, and pulling away from people are the red flags we look out for.

question: A patient has been convulsing for eight minutes straight without waking up. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Wait quietly at the bedside until the patient stops moving on their own
options.B: Have the patient stand up and walk around to clear their head
options.C: Call for emergency medical help and prepare airway support and rescue medication
options.D: Ask the family members what the patient ate for breakfast

explanation: This is a true emergency! Prolonged seizures cut off vital oxygen to the brain, so you need to sound the alarm and grab rescue medication right away.

question: What is the simple definition of a nutrient?

options.A: Artificial supplements created in laboratories to boost immunity
options.B: Medical drugs prescribed strictly to cure infectious diseases
options.C: Waste products that the human digestive system must eliminate
options.D: Chemical substances obtained from food for body function and repair

explanation: Nutrients are simply the helpful components we get from our food that keep us growing, energized, and healing properly!

question: What part do environmental factors play in kicking off an autoimmune disease?

options.A: They directly replace damaged genes in the bone marrow
options.B: They cure chronic inflammation by boosting white blood cells
options.C: They prevent the formation of autoantibodies
options.D: They can act as triggers that awaken an underlying immune vulnerability

explanation: Think of genetics as the loaded gun, and environmental triggers—like a nasty infection or stress—as the finger pulling the trigger.

question: A ward tries a new handwashing protocol. After one month, how do they check if it's working?

options.A: Assume it's working because nobody complained at the meeting
options.B: Compare current audit data against the baseline measurements taken before starting
options.C: Wait five years before checking infection stats
options.D: Ask the head nurse if the ward looks cleaner

explanation: Brilliant! You always compare your current results to your original baseline. Numbers don't lie, and it's the only way to prove real progress.

question: Why does a baby facing forward (occiput posterior position) often cause a long labour?

options.A: It softens the cervix too early before contractions even begin.
options.B: It forces a wider diameter of the fetal head to fit through the pelvic dimensions.
options.C: It immediately causes the placenta to detach from the uterine wall.
options.D: It completely stops the mother from breathing deeply during contractions.

explanation: Well done. When the baby's head faces the mum's tummy instead of her back, it cannot squeeze through the pelvis as easily, causing a traffic jam!

question: What is the main goal of community engagement in reproductive health?

options.A: Training foreign doctors to work in local clinics
options.B: Building more hospitals in rural communities
options.C: Reducing the cost of medical equipment importation
options.D: Involving local people directly in addressing health issues

explanation: Community engagement focuses on working side by side with local populations so they can actively shape health interventions that affect them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h1)

question: A 10-day-old baby has mild eyelid swelling and watery discharge. Which germ is most likely the cause?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Silver nitrate drops
options.C: Escherichia coli
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: Spot on! Chlamydia tends to show up a bit later than gonorrhea—usually between 5 and 14 days after birth. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: Why are primary health care nurses usually the ones doing community counselling?

options.A: They are often the first point of contact for community members
options.B: They have legal authority to prescribe psychiatric drugs
options.C: They have specialized degrees in clinical psychology
options.D: They spend most of their time in large urban hospitals

explanation: Because primary care nurses work right in the community, people naturally trust them and turn to them first for help.

question: A patient suffers a stroke affecting their left frontal lobe. What problem are they most likely to experience?

options.A: Loss of feeling in the lower legs
options.B: Difficulty speaking or forming words
options.C: Inability to hear simple sounds
options.D: Total blindness in both eyes

explanation: The frontal lobe houses motor control areas, including the region responsible for producing speech. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the anatomical term for the neck region?

options.A: Thoracic
options.B: Cephalic
options.C: Cervical
options.D: Lumbar

explanation: The neck is anatomically referred to as the cervical region, linking the head to the chest. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h2)

question: A patient with severe liver disease looks restless, seems confused, and has a fast heart rate with dropping blood pressure. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a comprehensive assessment for internal bleeding and report changes immediately
options.B: Document the findings in the chart and schedule a routine check for the next morning
options.C: Apply warm compresses to the patient's limbs to improve peripheral circulation
options.D: Encourage the patient to get out of bed and walk around the ward to ease restlessness

explanation: Restlessness, confusion, and dropping vitals are classic red flags! They can mean internal bleeding is happening, which needs urgent action.

question: Which route of administration is best for treating a sudden, life-threatening allergic reaction?

options.A: Inhaled powder
options.B: Oral tablet
options.C: Topical cream
options.D: Intravenous

explanation: Spot on! The intravenous (IV) route pushes the medication straight into the bloodstream for instant action during emergencies.

question: What is the primary goal of conducting regular nursing assessments in an adult day care setting?

options.A: To establish health baselines and catch subtle changes early
options.B: To enforce strict institutional rules upon the clients
options.C: To diagnose complex mental health disorders independently
options.D: To permanently replace the client's primary care physician

explanation: Regular assessments help nurses monitor chronic conditions and identify early signs of physical or cognitive deterioration before they become acute emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h4)

question: Which of these counts as skilled nursing care at home?

options.A: Purchasing groceries from the local market
options.B: Sweeping and cleaning the patient's bedroom
options.C: Cooking meals for the entire household
options.D: Changing a complex surgical wound dressing

explanation: Spot on! Skilled nursing involves clinical procedures like wound care that require professional nursing training.

question: Why do nurses check blood sugar in patients without known diabetes who suddenly become confused?

options.A: To rule out abnormal blood sugar as the cause
options.B: To check long-term diet compliance
options.C: To calculate daily calorie needs
options.D: To confirm chronic kidney failure

explanation: Changes in blood sugar can mess with brain function quickly. Checking it helps you figure out if confusion is coming from a high or low glucose level!

question: What usually triggers a flexor or withdrawal reflex?

options.A: An increase in body temperature during physical exercise
options.B: A painful stimulus such as stepping on a sharp object
options.C: A sudden stretch caused by lifting a heavy object
options.D: A gentle tap on a tendon to test joint movement

explanation: Flexor reflexes are our automatic survival responses. When something hurts—like stepping on a pin—you pull away before you even have time to think about it.

question: What is the primary function of the male reproductive system?

options.A: Filter waste products from the blood
options.B: Produce, sustain, and transport sperm
options.C: Digest complex dietary proteins
options.D: Regulate total body water balance

explanation: The primary role of the male reproductive system is the creation and delivery of sperm cells for reproduction alongside hormone production. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h1)

question: A patient who just had lung surgery is scared to cough because their incision hurts. What should you, the nurse, do first?

options.A: Tell the patient that coughing is optional and let them sleep all day.
options.B: Apply a tight chest binder to completely immobilize the chest wall.
options.C: Administer prescribed pain medication before encouraging controlled coughing exercises.
options.D: Report the patient immediately to the surgeon for emergency re-operation.

explanation: Wonderful clinical judgment! Controlling the pain first allows the patient to cough and clear their lungs safely without agony, preventing complications like collapsed lung areas.

question: Where are the free nerve endings that pick up pain mostly found?

options.A: Blood vessels
options.B: Sweat glands
options.C: Epidermis
options.D: Hypodermis

explanation: Well done! These free nerve endings stretch right up into the epidermis so they can easily catch superficial pain and temperature shifts.

question: Which parts of the body usually show the earliest physical signs of a nutrient deficiency?

options.A: Internal organs like the liver, kidneys, and pancreas
options.B: Rapid-turnover tissues like skin, hair, and mucous membranes
options.C: Dense connective tissues like cartilage and deep ligaments
options.D: Structural elements like cortical bone and long bones

explanation: Tissues that grow and shed quickly need a constant supply of nutrients, so they show signs of trouble first when supplies run low.

question: What is a major *indirect* cost associated with a physical disability?

options.A: The retail price of a custom wheelchair
options.B: Lost income due to unemployment and workplace barriers
options.C: Direct consultation fees at the clinic
options.D: Buying prescription anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation: Indirect costs are about what you *fail to earn* because of missed work, job loss, or barriers to employment—not direct store purchases.

question: Why is it so dangerous to mix sleeping pills with alcohol?

options.A: It causes immediate and irreversible liver failure within one hour
options.B: It neutralizes the medication, rendering the patient completely sleepless
options.C: It leads to profound respiratory depression and coma due to additive central nervous system suppression
options.D: It triggers severe high blood pressure and sudden stroke

explanation: Both alcohol and sleeping pills slow down your brain. Mixing them doubles up that depressing effect, which can easily stop a person's breathing.

question: What happens when one system, like local transport, breaks down in a community?

options.A: The cultural values of the residents immediately change
options.B: It negatively affects other systems, such as patient access to healthcare
options.C: Other social systems automatically stop functioning permanently
options.D: The geographical boundaries of the community shift eastward

explanation: Everything is connected! If transport fails, sick people might struggle to reach the clinic on time.

question: Why is mixing a sedative with alcohol so dangerous?

options.A: Combining them stops the digestive tract from absorbing any nutrients
options.B: The mixture causes an immediate and permanent increase in blood pressure
options.C: Both substances depress the central nervous system and multiply each other's effects
options.D: Alcohol instantly neutralizes the sedative, causing severe toxic shock in the liver

explanation: Both alcohol and sedatives slow down brain function. Combined, they team up to dangerously depress breathing and heart rate. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why are young married girls at such high risk for severe anxiety and depression?

options.A: Hormonal shifts during puberty completely prevent emotional stability
options.B: Cultural traditions mandate that they remain sad for the first year
options.C: Their brains naturally produce fewer mood-regulating chemicals
options.D: They face sudden social isolation, loss of family support, and domestic pressure

explanation: Spot on. Being cut off from friends and school, then thrust into heavy adult duties without emotional readiness, causes immense psychological distress.

question: What should a patient with a respiratory infection wear when moving outside their isolation room?

options.A: Cover the patient completely with a sterile plastic sheet
options.B: Transport the patient only during night shift hours
options.C: Ensure the patient walks without any staff assistance
options.D: Have the patient wear a surgical mask during transport

explanation: Exactly! Having the patient wear a mask traps any stray respiratory droplets right at the source while you walk them through the hospital corridors.

question: Which symptom should a nurse teach a patient with dysmenorrhoea to report immediately?

options.A: Feeling tired and needing extra sleep during bleeding
options.B: Mild lower abdominal cramping on the first day of menses
options.C: Sudden high fever and foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.D: A slight decrease in appetite during the menstrual cycle

explanation: You got it! Fever and foul discharge are red flags for an infection, which means it's not just regular period pain and needs urgent attention.

question: What is the main job of salivary amylase in your mouth?

options.A: Breaking down complex starches into simpler sugars
options.B: Killing all harmful bacteria entering the throat
options.C: Lubricating the food so it can slide down the throat
options.D: Neutralizing strong acids coming up from the stomach

explanation: Salivary amylase is a helpful little enzyme that gets a head start on digesting carbohydrates right while you chew your food.

question: Which feature is a must-have for a true experimental research design?

options.A: Observation of natural behaviors
options.B: Random assignment of participants
options.C: Qualitative interview transcripts
options.D: Retrospective chart reviews

explanation: For an experiment to be truly 'true,' you need to randomly assign people to groups, actively change an independent variable, and have a control group to compare them against.

question: How does assertive behavior differ from aggressive behavior?

options.A: Assertiveness requires shouting to be heard clearly
options.B: Aggression is used exclusively by senior nursing staff
options.C: Assertiveness attacks the issue rather than the person
options.D: Aggression always leads to better patient outcomes

explanation: While aggression targets and belittles individuals, assertiveness keeps the focus firmly on solving the professional problem. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h1)

question: What is the most important feature of a good surgical instrument wrap?

options.A: It must change color to black when exposed to sunlight
options.B: It must completely block all air and moisture permanently
options.C: It must let the sterilizing agent in while blocking microbes
options.D: It must dissolve in water during the washing cycle

explanation: A good wrap has a clever design: it lets steam or gas pass through to clean the tools, but keeps tiny bacteria out after the process is done.

question: What is a major goal of skilled care when looking after someone with a long-term, chronic illness?

options.A: Elimination of all daily living assistance needs.
options.B: Complete permanent cure of the underlying disease.
options.C: Immediate discharge back to independent living.
options.D: Stabilization, symptom relief, and functional preservation.

explanation: When a chronic condition can't be cured, our goal shifts to keeping the patient comfortable, managing symptoms, and helping them stay as active as possible.

question: What does Gross National Product (GNP) measure?

options.A: The total amount of physical cash printed by the central bank
options.B: Only the money earned by foreign companies inside the country
options.C: The total cost of running public hospitals for one year
options.D: The total economic value produced by a country's citizens globally

explanation: Think of GNP as tracking the wealth created by a country's people, no matter where in the world they are working! You've got this.

question: Which part of the joint capsule is responsible for making synovial fluid?

options.A: Synovial membrane
options.B: Periosteum
options.C: Fibrous layer
options.D: Articular cartilage

explanation: Correct! The inner lining of the joint capsule is the synovial membrane, and it constantly produces that slippery lubricating fluid.

question: What is the main difference between GDP and GNP?

options.A: GDP is calculated monthly while GNP is calculated every decade
options.B: GDP includes inflation while GNP excludes all taxes
options.C: GDP measures health services while GNP measures manufactured goods
options.D: GDP uses geographic location while GNP uses ownership and citizenship

explanation: The core distinction is simple: GDP cares about where production happens, while GNP cares about who owns the production.

question: What does a 'just culture' in nursing try to balance?

options.A: Accountability for choices with understanding of system flaws
options.B: Zero documentation with total reliance on verbal handovers
options.C: Strict punishment for every single near miss that occurs
options.D: Financial profit margins with patient satisfaction scores

explanation: A just culture is fair: it holds people responsible for reckless choices, but supports them when honest human errors or system flaws happen.

question: How is toxicology different from standard pharmacology?

options.A: Toxicology focuses specifically on harmful effects and poisons
options.B: Toxicology deals exclusively with the retail pricing of drugs
options.C: Toxicology only studies medications derived from synthetic chemicals
options.D: Toxicology examines how plant roots are crushed for remedies

explanation: Great job! While pharmacology studies all drug actions, toxicology zooms in strictly on poisons and harmful reactions.

question: You check a patient's blood pressure during a routine community outreach. Which level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Spot-on! Screening tests like blood pressure checks catch hidden problems early. That is the exact definition of secondary prevention.

question: What does the term 'stricture' mean when talking about urinary tract injuries?

options.A: A complete widening of the bladder wall from excessive urine pressure
options.B: A narrowing of a tubular structure like the urethra caused by scar tissue
options.C: The sudden permanent cessation of urine production in both kidneys
options.D: An abnormal connection between the bowel and the urinary bladder

explanation: A stricture happens when scar tissue forms as an injury heals, pinching the tube (like the urethra) so it becomes too narrow for urine to flow easily.

question: What does the letter 'D' stand for in the ABCDE primary survey?

options.A: Disability
options.B: Diagnosis
options.C: Dehydration
options.D: Diet

explanation: In the emergency ABCDE framework, D stands for disability, which evaluates basic neurological status. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T2#GNS315_U3_T2_h2)

question: In what kind of situation would an intracardiac injection most likely be considered?

options.A: Before taking a patient for a scheduled X-ray scan
options.B: When treating mild high blood pressure in the clinic
options.C: During routine morning medication rounds on a stable ward
options.D: During severe cardiac arrest when standard IV access fails

explanation: Spot on! This high-risk technique is saved strictly for dire emergency resuscitation when no other way to give medicine is available.

question: Why is extra care needed when a hospital outsources clinical services like labs or radiology?

options.A: External vendors are completely exempt from local health and safety regulations
options.B: Nurses no longer need to document patient histories or treatment results
options.C: Patient safety and diagnostic accuracy directly depend on maintaining high clinical standards
options.D: Non-clinical staff can easily perform these procedures without professional training

explanation: Because clinical work directly affects patient lives, hospitals must keep a close eye on quality even when an outside vendor is helping out.

question: Which of the following is an indirect method to assess medication adherence?

options.A: Checking tissue biopsies for microscopic drug deposits
options.B: Analyzing urine specimens for active chemical traces
options.C: Counting the remaining pills in the medicine bottle
options.D: Measuring exact drug metabolites in a blood sample

explanation: Pill counts, patient interviews, and refill records are indirect ways to check compliance without laboratory drug assays. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is family planning considered a key pillar of safe motherhood?

options.A: It helps women space pregnancies to protect their physical health
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory tests during pregnancy
options.C: It completely stops women from experiencing menopause
options.D: It guarantees that every baby born will be a male child

explanation: Giving mum's body time to rest and rebuild strength between babies means a healthier mother and a safer next pregnancy!

question: What is the most common spark that sets off a sudden metabolic or endocrine emergency?

options.A: A sudden physical stressor or infection
options.B: A sudden drop in room temperature
options.C: Drinking too much water too fast
options.D: Eating too much high-fat food

explanation: You've got this! When infections or physical stress hit the body, they demand extra energy, easily pushing a delicate hormone balance right over the edge into an emergency.

question: What's the main difference between accounting and budgeting in healthcare?

options.A: Accounting is handled exclusively by nurses while budgeting is done by doctors.
options.B: Accounting focuses only on nursing salaries while budgeting tracks patient medications.
options.C: Accounting is a short-term daily task while budgeting is only done every ten years.
options.D: Accounting looks at past financial records while budgeting plans for future financial needs.

explanation: Think of accounting as looking in the rearview mirror at what you've already spent, while budgeting is looking through the windshield to plan what's ahead!

question: Why does the human body require a dual-circuit vascular system?

options.A: To ensure that blood flows in both directions simultaneously in arteries
options.B: To prevent high blood pressure from damaging delicate skin tissues
options.C: To allow the heart to rest while the lungs pump blood independently
options.D: To separate oxygenated blood from deoxygenated blood efficiently

explanation: Separating the pulmonary and systemic circuits ensures that oxygen-rich blood is kept distinct from oxygen-depleted blood for maximum delivery efficiency. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is a direct clinical result of long-term drug non-compliance in chronic illnesses?

options.A: Immediate and permanent cure of the medical condition
options.B: Worsening of the disease and potential organ damage
options.C: Stable laboratory test results over many months
options.D: Strengthening of the immune system against infections

explanation: Without steady medication, chronic diseases progress unchecked, eventually destroying vital organs like the heart and kidneys. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h3)

question: What should a nurse researcher do if their new results don't match older studies?

options.A: Hide the contradictory data so the paper gets published
options.B: Explore potential reasons for the differences in findings
options.C: Change the original hypothesis to match the old literature
options.D: Assume all previous researchers made mistakes in math

explanation: Exactly! Science grows when we look closely at *why* results differ—maybe times have changed, or the patient group is different.

question: A patient drinks a six-ounce cup of juice. How many milliliters should the nurse record on the chart?

options.A: 60 milliliters
options.B: 180 milliliters
options.C: 300 milliliters
options.D: 120 milliliters

explanation: Multiplying six ounces by thirty milliliters per ounce gives a total volume of 180 milliliters. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why is it important to quickly report and investigate serious adverse events following immunization (AEFIs)?

options.A: To increase the total number of children attending clinic
options.B: To protect public confidence and maintain safety standards
options.C: To eliminate the need for cold chain temperature logs
options.D: To ensure that nurses receive financial compensation

explanation: Acting fast and being transparent stops panic, squashes false rumors, and keeps trust high in our healthcare services.

question: A client who was alert yesterday suddenly struggles to remember where they are and cannot focus on questions. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: A sudden change in mental status that needs immediate reporting
options.B: Normal tiredness that will go away after a long afternoon nap
options.C: A permanent personality change caused by old age
options.D: A sign that the client no longer needs any nursing care

explanation: Acute confusion or declining mental status in a neurologic client is a red flag that requires prompt investigation and reporting. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to using living wills in clinical practice?

options.A: Vaguely written instructions like 'no heroic measures'
options.B: Having too many copies of the document easily available to doctors
options.C: Family members disputing the wishes during an emergency
options.D: Documents being left at home instead of brought to the hospital

explanation: Having too many accessible copies is rarely a problem; the usual issue is that documents are hidden at home or poorly written. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h6)

question: Which mental health issue is most commonly diagnosed in survivors of severe violence?

options.A: Bipolar mood disorder
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
options.D: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)

explanation: Correct! Survivors of intense physical, emotional, or sexual trauma very often develop PTSD because of the deep impact of their experience.

question: What is the biggest cause of antimicrobial resistance today?

options.A: Misuse and overuse of antimicrobial drugs
options.B: Routine handwashing with antibacterial soap
options.C: Complete adherence to vaccination schedules
options.D: Strict adherence to sterile surgical techniques

explanation: Exactly right! Taking antibiotics when we don't need them—or not finishing the full dose—teaches germs how to survive our drugs.

question: Why do active tissues like tumors absorb large amounts of FDG during a PET scan?

options.A: Rapidly dividing cells require high amounts of energy and glucose.
options.B: Cancer cells have abnormal blood vessels that block normal water flow.
options.C: The radioactive tracer binds directly to the DNA strands of damaged cells.
options.D: Tumors actively attract and trap radioactive metal inside their walls.

explanation: Exactly! Because cancer cells grow and multiply so fast, they need a ton of energy. Since FDG acts just like glucose, the tumor sucks it right up, making it glow brightly on the scan.

question: Which common infection is most often responsible for scarring the fallopian tubes and causing female infertility?

options.A: Candida albicans
options.B: Chlamydia trachomatis
options.C: Human papillomavirus
options.D: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation: You nailed it! Sexually transmitted infections like chlamydia can cause silent infections that quietly damage the delicate lining of the tubes. Great job staying sharp on clinical facts!

question: Which hormone gets released when fats and proteins show up in the small intestine?

options.A: Cholecystokinin
options.B: Aldosterone
options.C: Erythropoietin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Cholecystokinin (let's just call it CCK!) is the hormone that shouts to the gallbladder and pancreas: 'Hey, fatty food has arrived, time to release your juices!'

question: What is usually at the root of organizational conflict?

options.A: Patients refusing to take medication
options.B: A nurse having low self-esteem
options.C: Systemic issues and structural policies
options.D: Personal dislikes between two nurses

explanation: Organizational conflict stems from institutional rules, budgets, and structures rather than personal beefs.

question: Why must medical waste be burned in an incinerator or buried deep instead of going to a normal dump?

options.A: It is required to generate electricity for local hospitals
options.B: It eliminates the need for any kind of protective clothing
options.C: It prevents injuries and the spread of infectious pathogens
options.D: It turns hazardous waste into edible organic fertilizer

explanation: Well done! Hospital waste carries germs and sharps that can easily harm waste workers and the community if not safely destroyed.

question: What is the primary role of a nurse acting as a patient advocate?

options.A: Refusing to talk with doctors about care plans
options.B: Suing the hospital administration whenever there is a treatment delay
options.C: Protecting the patient's rights, safety, and dignity when they cannot speak for themselves
options.D: Making all final medical decisions on behalf of the family

explanation: Brilliant! Being an advocate means standing up for your patients and keeping their best interests at heart.

question: What kind of vaginal odor is classically tied to bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: No odor at all
options.B: Sweet fruit odor
options.C: Musty bread odor
options.D: Fishy odor

explanation: You got it. The chemical byproducts created by those extra anaerobic bacteria give off a distinct fishy smell. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h4)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with severe lower right chest pain after a motorcycle fall. Which test is the doctor likely to order first?

options.A: Chest X-ray
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Urinalysis
options.D: Lumbar puncture

explanation: After chest trauma, an X-ray is the quickest way to check for broken ribs or bruised lungs. You're building great clinical instincts!

question: Which structural feature is found in spongy bone instead of compact bone?

options.A: Trabeculae
options.B: Concentric lamellae
options.C: Haversian canals
options.D: Osteons

explanation: Spongy bone is made of a porous network of struts and plates called trabeculae, lacking standard osteon cylinders. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h6)

question: What must a cell do if it makes steroid hormones and suddenly receives a continuous call to release more?

options.A: It must rapidly synthesize new hormone molecules from cholesterol on the spot
options.B: It pumps stored hormones out of the cytoplasm using ATP energy channels
options.C: It opens storage vesicle gates to release a large backup supply of ready hormones
options.D: It stops producing hormones until old supplies are cleared from the blood

explanation: Unlike peptide hormones, steroid hormones aren't stored in large stockpiles. If the body needs more right now, the cell has to manufacture them fresh from cholesterol immediately.

question: What do we call the type of laryngoscopy that uses a thin, flexible camera passed through the nose?

options.A: Indirect mirror laryngoscopy
options.B: Open surgical laryngoscopy
options.C: Rigid direct laryngoscopy
options.D: Fiberoptic laryngoscopy

explanation: You got it! A fiberoptic scope uses a flexible, thin camera that slides easily through the nose while the patient is awake.

question: How does an emotionally intelligent nurse leader handle a dispute between two staff members?

options.A: By publicly reprimanding both nurses during the morning handover meeting
options.B: By immediately issuing formal query letters without discussing the root cause
options.C: By ignoring the dispute and hoping the nurses resolve it on their own
options.D: By listening to both sides calmly and guiding them toward a constructive resolution

explanation: Great choice! An emotionally intelligent leader uses patience and communication to solve conflicts and keep the team spirit high.

question: What is the main goal of using the 'teach-back' method with a patient?

options.A: To replace the need for written discharge leaflets
options.B: To fulfill mandatory hospital documentation quotas
options.C: To test the patient's ability to read medical textbooks
options.D: To verify that the patient truly understood the instructions

explanation: Asking them to explain your instructions back in their own words helps you catch any misunderstandings before they go home.

question: Which two hormones play the biggest role in helping uterine fibroids grow?

options.A: FSH and LH
options.B: Insulin and glucagon
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Estrogen and progesterone

explanation: Estrogen and progesterone fuel the growth of these muscle cells. That is why fibroids are so closely tied to a woman's reproductive years!

question: What type of exercise is especially great for helping men fight off muscle loss during andropause?

options.A: Breathing exercises
options.B: Flexibility stretching
options.C: Passive range of motion
options.D: Resistance training

explanation: Lifting weights or doing resistance work helps build strength and fights off the natural muscle and bone loss that comes with lower testosterone.

question: When does the first stage of labour officially come to an end?

options.A: When regular uterine contractions first begin
options.B: When the baby's head emerges from the vagina
options.C: When the placenta is successfully delivered
options.D: When the cervix is fully dilated at 10 centimeters

explanation: Stage one is all about opening the cervix. Once it hits 10 cm, that stage is wrapped up and it's time to push!

question: Some food handlers are struggling with hygiene rules because they find English difficult. What should the nurse supervisor do?

options.A: Stop doing hygiene training and rely only on surprise inspections
options.B: Punish the workers for failing to read the English instruction manual
options.C: Conduct training sessions using the local language and visual demonstrations
options.D: Report the workers to the police for breaking environmental laws

explanation: Adapting how you teach to match your audience ensures everyone understands these life-saving safety practices. Great clinical judgment!
